title: Security governance, ephemerality, KMS and ISO/SOC2 walkthrough
topics: Data residency and private deployment options
summary: Customer asked for explicit guarantees around prompt ephemerality, SOC2/ISO evidence, and KMS-based encryption. Redwood AE/SE explained hosted vs private tradeoffs, RBAC/SSO options, audit log granularity, and provided next steps to share artifacts and schedule a pilot scoping.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. we'll run through security and governance, and Oren will jump into more of the KMS and architecture.
[00:00:08] Lena Ortiz: Hi, thanks. We've got Amir and Sofia as well, we're mainly focused on three things: no-training confirmation, how long prompts are retained, and KMS integration.
[00:00:20] Oren Patel: Great, yeah we'll cover that. quick note, apologies in advance if the auto transcript mangles some acronyms, sometimes SAML turns into, uh, 'sam-el' in the script.
[00:00:30] Dr. Amir Khan: that's fine. um, first, do you have a hard policy that customer prompts are never used to train models? we need that in writing for our privacy team.
[00:00:41] Maya Chen: yes, short answer: Redwood does not use customer prompt or content for model training. longer answer: hosted offering processes requests transiently and we can commit to no training on customer data; we also have options to disable retention at the route level.
[00:00:56] Sofia Alvarez: Can you point us to the clause or attestation? Legal needs an auditable statement.
[00:01:03] Maya Chen: we'll send the formal no-train attestation and the clause we recommend adding to contracts. we'll also include SOC 2 Type II report that covers data handling controls.
[00:01:12] Lena Ortiz: Great. about retention — what's the default, and can we enforce zero retention for our workloads?
[00:01:20] Oren Patel: Default is 30 days for some operational logs, but content retention for downstream dev/quality is off by default for enterprise customers — you can request ephemerality, which ensures prompt content is not stored beyond in-memory processing. for stricter controls we recommend Redwood Private or a Dedicated setup with VPC and bring-your-own-keys.
[00:01:39] Dr. Amir Khan: So ephemerality means no disk writes of prompt bodies, only ephemeral KV in memory?
[00:01:44] Oren Patel: correct, we avoid storing prompt text in persistent storage. we do persist metadata for billing and audit (request id, model, token counts), but not the full prompt if ephemerality is enabled.
[00:01:55] Lena Ortiz: about metadata, what fields are included? we need to know if any PII could leak via headers or metadata.
[00:02:02] Oren Patel: metadata is minimal: request id, timestamp, model id, token counts, routing decision. headers that include PII are redacted by default, but you should avoid sending PHI in headers.
[00:02:13] Sofia Alvarez: What about audit logs? we need per-request audit trails with user identifiers and action names for our auditors.
[00:02:20] Maya Chen: audit logs can be pushed to your SIEM via our cloud export or delivered into a customer-owned bucket. logs include request id, redwood user id (if using RBAC tokens), model used, latency, and disposition (accepted/failed). we can configure retention windows to match your compliance needs.
[00:02:36] Lena Ortiz: Encryption — do you offer envelope encryption and KMS integration? we require customer-managed keys for production data.
[00:02:44] Oren Patel: yes, we support envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). keys are used for data-at-rest and for encrypting persisted caches; live in-memory operations are unencrypted for low-latency but those are never written to disk when ephemerality is on.
[00:03:00] Dr. Amir Khan: what about key rotation? is rotation seamless?
[00:03:05] Oren Patel: we support scheduled rotation and we provide a rotation policy sample; re-encryption of persisted objects is handled via background jobs — we'll share the runbook.
[00:03:14] Lena Ortiz: network controls: can we require egress only to certain endpoints, VPC peering, or private link like setups?
[00:03:21] Maya Chen: yes, Dedicated and Private support VPC peering and private link. hosted customers get region restrictions and IP allowlists. for most sensitive data we recommend Private deployment with customer-controlled network.
[00:03:33] Sofia Alvarez: SOC 2 and ISO — do you have attestations? we need the latest reports and the scope.
[00:03:40] Maya Chen: we have SOC 2 Type II covering the hosted platform and operational controls — we'll provide the report. ISO 27001 certificate is available for our control plane — again we'll share the scope doc.
[00:03:51] Dr. Amir Khan: Are there any exceptions in SOC coverage for model training or 3rd-party subprocessors?
[00:03:57] Maya Chen: model training on customer data is explicitly excluded from our practices; we don't train on customer content. subprocessors are listed in the AUP, and we disclose them in the DPIA; we'll send the subprocessor list.
[00:04:09] Lena Ortiz: On SSO — we use SAML + SCIM for provisioning. can we integrate RBAC into API tokens so our users have scoped access?
[00:04:18] Oren Patel: yes, we integrate with SSO for console access and SCIM for provisioning. API tokens can be scoped to roles; you can tie tokens to projects, restrict model families, set per-token rate limits, and enforce TTLs.
[00:04:30] Sofia Alvarez: Do tokens appear in logs? we need to make sure tokens aren't stored in plain text.
[00:04:35] Oren Patel: tokens are hashed in our systems, logs reference token id hashes not raw secrets. we also support short-lived tokens and rotation.
[00:04:44] Lena Ortiz: can you support a contractual 'no retention except for audit metadata' clause?
[00:04:50] Maya Chen: yes — we provide standard contract language; for enterprise deals we'll add explicit ephemerality clauses and the KMS BYOK terms.
[00:04:58] Dr. Amir Khan: quick question on PHI: if our app returns a patient identifier in model output, is Redwood responsible for that?
[00:05:06] Maya Chen: we process what you send; customer is responsible for the content you submit. we do provide controls to minimize risk: output filters, PII redaction options, and ability to disable model logging.
[00:05:18] Lena Ortiz: About retention policies: can we set retention per-route? we have different routes, some for anonymized logs, some for sensitive QA.
[00:05:26] Oren Patel: yes per-route retention settings are supported in the console and via config APIs. default retention can be overridden per route.
[00:05:32] Sofia Alvarez: How is 'ephemerality' audited? we need evidence that content wasn't persisted.
[00:05:38] Maya Chen: we can provide audit trails showing storage operations for requests and a signed attestation for ephemerality configurations. for Private deployments you can run local audits.
[00:05:49] Dr. Amir Khan: operational question — if you fall back to a cheaper model in a region due to capacity, is the fallback model data handling the same?
[00:05:57] Oren Patel: it depends; fallback models are compatible from a policy standpoint — our no-train policy applies platform-wide — but we will disclose any model variant differences in the baseline security doc.
[00:06:08] Lena Ortiz: Are there any third parties that could see content unencrypted?
[00:06:12] Maya Chen: not in normal operation. subprocessors may have access to infrastructure logs; we include subprocessors in the DPA and provide SOC coverage where applicable.
[00:06:22] Sofia Alvarez: will you share the DPA and subprocessors list?
[00:06:25] Maya Chen: yes, will include with the SOC/ISO pack.
[00:06:29] [00:30:00] -- (omitted middle minute-markers, continuing key exchanges) --
[00:40:10] Oren Patel: (deep dive) here's how the KMS envelope works: customer key wraps the data encryption key (DEK) used for persisted caches and backups; ephemeral memory operations never touch DEKs on disk when ephemerality is enabled.
[00:40:25] Lena Ortiz: technical ask: we want sample logs 'csv' showing columns we would get for SIEM ingestion; can you provide that?
[00:40:30] Oren Patel: yes, sample log schema and a demo payload will be attached.
[00:40:35] Dr. Amir Khan: and a diagram of key flow please, the rotation steps.
[00:40:39] Oren Patel: will include a runbook and rotation policy.
[00:45:00] Sofia Alvarez: we'll need a legal review of the no-train attestation — include the exact signature block.
[00:45:06] Maya Chen: will do.
[00:45:12] Lena Ortiz: last question: if we do a Private deployment, can we confirm that model weights and training infra are completely isolated?
[00:45:20] Oren Patel: Private deployment isolates inference runtime and model artifacts; by default we run with customer-controlled storage for artifacts and you can opt to host model weights in your own registry. we'll scope that in the pilot.
[00:45:33] Maya Chen: okay, quick recap — we'll send: SOC 2 Type II, ISO attestation, DPA/subprocessor list, no-train attestation, KMS architecture diagram, sample logs, and retention config steps.
[00:45:45] Lena Ortiz: timeline?
[00:45:47] Maya Chen: we'll aim to send the docs by Friday 2026-11-27. Oren will follow up with the diagrams and runbook by Monday 2026-11-30.
[00:45:58] Sofia Alvarez: thanks everyone.
[00:46:02] Dr. Amir Khan: thanks.
[00:46:05] Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll set up the pilot scoping next week. bye.
next_steps: Maya to send SOC 2 Type II report, ISO attestation, and pen-test summary by 2026-11-27
Oren to share architecture diagram showing KMS envelope and VPC option by 2026-11-30
HeliosCare legal to confirm PHI whitelist and retention window (Lena/Sofia) by 2026-12-02
Schedule follow-up pilot kickoff for private deployment scoping week of 2026-12-08

Oren Patel; Share KMS integration diagram and sample key rotation policy; due 2026-11-30
Lena Ortiz; Provide PHI whitelist and expected retention windows; due 2026-12-02
